detail: At 7,580.07 the S&P 500 is about 3.4% below its 52-week closing high of 7,844.52, after its worst day since June on Friday. Pullbacks of a few per cent happen several times in a typical year; for a long-term investor they are normal weather, not a signal.
source: AP closing figures via Yahoo Finance, 30 Oct (high from Reuters, 29 Oct)

detail: On Thursday rising Nasdaq stocks narrowly beat fallers (2,464 to 2,308), yet the index fell 1.4% because a few giants like Alphabet dropped hard; 191 stocks hit 52-week lows against 88 highs. When most shares rise but the index falls, it shows how much a handful of huge companies steer it.

The US 10-year yield edged down to about 4.93% on Friday as investors sold shares. Safe government bonds paying close to 5% set a high bar that shares have to beat, which is one reason pricey tech shares are being questioned.

Markets put about a 78% chance on a Fed rate rise on 9 December (down from 84%) and fully price a Bank of England rise from 3.75% to 4% next Thursday, 5 November. The ECB held at 2.50% on Thursday but left the door open to a December rise.
source: CappNotes (CME FedWatch) and Trading Economics, 29 Oct

detail: Brent slipped 0.4% to $114.88 a barrel as talk of US-Iran diplomacy and Europe's plan to release emergency reserves offset fresh supply worries. Dear oil keeps inflation high, which is the main reason central banks are leaning towards rate rises.
